boards.name: Adafruit Fruit Jam
boards.method: Build from source and program through SWD
boards.summary: This project's Fruit Jam SmallVM has physical SWD installation evidence. A CMSIS-DAP probe and RP2350-capable OpenOCD are the verified programming route.
steps: Confirm the Fruit Jam RP2350B board and matching debug connector. Preserve the existing image and program storage before replacement.
Build the Fruit Jam SmallVM target using its pinned Zephyr workspace and isolated Arduino module.
Follow the SWD wiring and update guide to program and verify the matching ELF. Keep application and saved-program regions separate.
Restart the board and verify its VM identity and USB connection. UF2 inspection alone does not establish a tested drag-and-drop or browser installation route.

release.label: Project releases
release.note: The reviewed project releases contain no ready-to-flash Fruit Jam SmallVM image. Build the matching board image from source.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-S3 RLCD 4.2
boards.method: Pinned Zephyr build and USB programming
boards.summary: The standalone ESP32-S3 RLCD target includes SmallVM v417 and has physical installation and runtime evidence. Installation uses host Zephyr/esptool tooling; this page does not flash USB.
steps: Use the exact ESP32-S3-RLCD-4.2 N16R8 target and the pinned workspace described in the board guide.
Build the standalone SmallVM profile with its verified VM/editor sources and your local private configuration.
Back up the selected board, identify its actual USB port and follow the documented download-mode, partition and west flash procedure.
Verify the VM and saved-program behavior after boot. Keep the generated private configuration and firmware backups local.

release.label: Project releases
release.note: The reviewed project releases contain no ready-to-flash ESP32-S3 RLCD SmallVM image. The installation route is a board-specific source build.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4 WIFI6
boards.method: Native Zephyr image with revision-guarded USB serial programming
boards.summary: The physically tested target is the 32 MiB revision 1.3/pre-v3 board. Its native simple-boot image uses offset 0x2000 and a revision guard. Installation is a host-tool procedure, separate from the editor's USB connection.
steps: Confirm the exact board and silicon revision, then preserve the current image and settings.
Build the pinned native Zephyr hpcore target and apply the documented image guard.

Follow the board guide's simple-boot layout and selected-device checks. The existing guarded helper is scoped to the documented COM5 CH343 workstation device; verify your own device before adapting that procedure.
Verify SmallVM over USB after boot. Companion C6 Wi-Fi commissioning is separate and remains incomplete.

sources.label: P4 build, image guard and USB installation

release.label: Project releases
release.note: The reviewed project releases contain no public ready-to-flash P4 SmallVM image. Build the matching revision-specific image; no browser flasher is offered here.

boards.name: SparkFun XRP RP2350
boards.method: Production RP2350B source build and SWD programming
boards.summary: The verified target is production ROB-26619 with RP2350B and RM2. The integrated SmallVM v417 image has physical SWD, USB and retention evidence. Motor and servo actions remain locked.
steps: Confirm the production controller and keep the motor supply off during installation. Preserve its current image, program and settings.
Follow the pinned XRP build guide, including its isolated Arduino module and reviewed radio configuration.
Use the positively identified SWD probe and RP2350 tools to program and verify the matching application image while preserving the settings/program tail.
Check VM identity, USB and retained state after boot. This installation guide does not unlock or validate robot movement.

sources.label: Production XRP build and retention guide

release.label: Project releases
release.note: The reviewed project releases contain no ready-to-flash production XRP SmallVM package. Use the production-board source build and verified programming procedure.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi 5
boards.summary: The current installer builds pinned native SmallVM v417, its local JavaScript editor and isolated Python/Blinka environment on the Pi. It is a Linux software installation, not USB firmware flashing.
steps: Use a Raspberry Pi 5 with current 64-bit Pi OS/Debian and the prerequisites listed in the source-installer guide.
Review and run the published install-pi5.sh bootstrap on the Pi as an ordinary account. Its downloaded source archive is pinned and hash-checked.
Choose foreground use or explicitly request a LAN/service setup. Existing unrelated services and occupied ports are preserved or refused.
Open the local editor URL printed by the installer, or use its documented SSH-tunnel route. The older alpha2 package below has a narrower feature set.

release.label: Older Pi 5 alpha2 release
release.note: A verified published ARM64 alpha2 package is available with its installer and SHA256SUMS. It predates the current source installer; follow its own release instructions and compatibility limits.

boards.name: MicroDuck RK3566
boards.summary: Physical robot commissioning and a compatible reviewed SmallVM release are pending. The portal editor is a disconnected preview. A Pi installation does not establish MicroDuck compatibility.
steps: Inventory the actual shipping OS, architecture, API version and existing robot services when hardware is available.
Follow the read-only commissioning and preflight guides, preserving the robot's existing services and identity checks.
Wait for a compatible reviewed release before installation. No install command or browser firmware writer is enabled by this page.
Begin real acceptance with the documented private editor and read-only gateway after those prerequisites are satisfied.

release.label: Project releases
release.note: No compatible MicroDuck installation package is present in the reviewed project releases. The Pi package and editor-preview archive are not MicroDuck firmware.

boards.name: Arduino UNO Q
boards.card_note: App Lab guide; editor reference only
boards.method: Separate App Lab application and MCU runtime installation
boards.summary: The separate UNO Q community project publishes v0.1.2 with an App Lab application and guarded STM32 runtime installation. Its bundled editor is legacy GP; this portal's JavaScript UNO Q profile remains an offline reference.
steps: Read the reference project's Start Here guide on UNO Q Linux and review the v0.1.2 community package.
Import its App Lab ZIP and preserve the original Linux LED state before the first App start.

Install the MCU runtime separately using the exact verified loader and application-only recovery procedure. The combined FPGA-preserving profile is physically tested; the generic profile was built but not physically installed.
Start the App and use the editor URL or tunnel described by that project. Normal App startup does not reinstall or reset the MCU.

release.label: UNO Q community v0.1.2 release
release.note: The verified release contains uno-q-microblocks-community-0.1.2.zip. Follow the separate project's instructions; it is not a browser USB flasher or a validated port of this portal's JavaScript editor.
